Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Status page update — elevated 502 errors impacting chat endpoints

Hi Evan / Talaria team,

We wanted to let you know we’ve posted an incident on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20261105-9

Summary: between ~08:45 and 09:02 PST we observed an elevated rate of 502 responses from the hosted Chat API (/v1/chat and websocket proxies). Root cause appears related to a cache migration job that increased load on the proxy layer and triggered a subset of upstream worker crashes.

Impact: partial errors for chat and conversational endpoints for ~18 minutes. Some requests returned 502s; the system automatically retried a portion of traffic, but customers using non-retry clients may have seen failed calls. No customer data was lost or mutated.

Mitigation: at 09:02 we rolled back the migration for the proxy cache layer; returned workers were healthy and error rates returned to baseline by ~09:10. We continue to monitor.

What we’re doing next:
- internal post-incident review and timeline (ETA for summary: tomorrow EOD PT)
- producing an itemized timeline for SLA/credit review
- follow-up remediation plan to prevent recurrence (config guardrails + controlled migration steps)

Attachment: statuspage-incident-1105-snapshot.png (image/png) — brief dashboard snapshot at 08:58 showing error spike.

Apologies for the disruption; I’ll follow up with a postmortem and a remediation plan. If you need help re-running any failed requests or want us to surface logs for specific request IDs, send a list and we’ll prioritize.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — Nov 5 elevated 502s (INC-20261105-9)

Hi Evan / Talaria team,

Thanks again for flagging this. Below is a concise post-incident summary and the next steps we’ve committed to. Full timeline and artifact links: https://app.redwood.ai/kibana/incident-1105 (internal) and https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20261105-9 (public).

Executive summary:
- Incident ID: INC-20261105-9
- Window: 2026-11-05T08:45:00-08:00 to 2026-11-05T09:10:00-08:00
- Impact: Elevated 502 errors affecting ~12% of Chat API requests globally; customers using simple clients without automatic retries saw failed calls. No persisted data loss or unauthorized access.

Root cause (short):
A cache migration job increased connection churn on the HTTP proxy pool. When a subset of proxy worker processes hit an unexpected load pattern, they crashed and returned 502 responses until the migration was rolled back. Marcus has a full technical write-up in the internal timeline.

Customer-specific notes for Brightleaf:
- We examined the two request IDs you provided: br-req-20261105-3a12 and br-req-20261105-3a73. Both requests received a 502 from the proxy; no duplicate downstream webhooks were triggered by Redwood. We confirmed payloads containing customer PII were not persisted in any worker logs beyond standard transient request logs; no PII exposure. (Dev Patel)

SLA & credits:
- Based on your usage and the incident window we’ll apply a pro-rata credit per the SLA. I’ve opened a billing request with Finance — reference: BL-INC-1105. We’ll send a formal credit memo by next week.

Remediations (short):
1) Add migration circuit-breaker to prevent simultaneous worker churn (owner: Marcus Lin, ETA: 2026-11-20)
2) Harden proxy autoscaling thresholds and improve health-check sensitivity (owner: Dev Patel, ETA: 2026-11-12)
3) Add a customer-facing retry guidance doc and SDK note recommending idempotent retries for non-critical calls (owner: Marissa Cole, ETA: 2026-11-15)

Attachments: incident-timeline-1105.pdf (application/pdf) — internal timeline and logs summary.

If you’d like us to re-run any throttled/failed requests as part of a remediation plan, let us know the IDs and preferred behavior (replay vs. manual re-trigger).

Apologies again for the disruption — we’re treating this as high priority and reporting back with progress on the items above.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
